question.worked_solution:
If $X$ follows a discrete uniform distribution over a set $S,$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{|S|}, & x\in S \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $X∼U\{2,3,4,…,11\},$ and the set $S=\{2,3,4,…,11\}$ has $|S|=11-2+1=10$ items. So, we have

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{10}, & x=2,3,4,…,11 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

In $S,$ the items that satisfy $X\ge 5$ are $5,6,7,…,11.$ There are $11-5+1=7$ of these items. Therefore,

$$
P(X\ge 5)=7\cdot \frac{1}{10}=\frac{7}{10}.
$$
